subject: Renewal & Capacity Expansion — Reserved Pool Commitment and token-rate assurance
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@dataspan.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Satsang <priya@dataspan.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + capacity increase — DataSpan

Evelyn,

We're getting close to the end of our current term (June 30) and we'd like to discuss the renewal. After load testing the model set for our next product release, we'll need to add capacity: roughly +8 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 class) behind a reserved pool.

Key asks from our side:
- Formal language in the renewal that commits to a minimum aggregate token-rate across the reserved pool (we use tokens/sec as our throughput metric).
- Clear SLOs for availability and a definition of how Redwood measures tokens/sec.
- Fallback behavior and overage rates if we spike above the guarantee.

Can you put together an initial commitment letter or addendum that we can review with Legal? We're open to a 12–24 month extension if the economics align.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Director of ML Ops | DataSpan, Inc.
oliver@dataspan.ai

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Satsang <priya@dataspan.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity increase — DataSpan

Oliver — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. We're excited to support your May/June launch.

Quick summary of what we'll propose in the renewal packet (draft attached):
- Reserved pool expansion: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs in your existing dedicated pool, capacity reserved for the 12-month term option (month-to-month on top if you prefer shorter).
- Token-rate assurance: commitment to an aggregate baseline of 250,000 tokens/sec measured at the reserved-pool ingress across the US region (definition and measurement window in Section 2).
- SLO: 99.9% monthly availability for the token-rate guarantee window; crediting and remedies spelled out in Section 4 (credits prorated by the shortfall percentage).
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to warm spare capacity in other compatible pool variants with graceful degradation rules; overage pricing at $0.012 per 1k tokens above the guaranteed rate (tiered).

I've attached a first-pass "DataSpan_Renewal_Commitment_Draft.pdf" and a more detailed "TokenRate_Addendum_v1.docx" that includes the SLO wording and instrumentation expectations (what metrics we expose in Console).

To move quickly: can we set a 30-min sync Thursday to run through the SLO wording and any procurement/legal constraints? If you approve the draft at a high level we'll route a DocuSign-ready addendum to you next week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

(Attachments: DataSpan_Renewal_Commitment_Draft.pdf, TokenRate_Addendum_v1.docx)

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@dataspan.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Satsang <priya@dataspan.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity increase — DataSpan

Thanks, Evelyn — draft looks promising. Couple of clarifying questions before Legal reviews:

1) Token-rate definition: Is the 250k tokens/sec aggregate measured as a 1-minute rolling average at the pool ingress or as an instantaneous TPS? We need the explicit sampling/aggregation window.
2) Per-model fairness: If we route to warm spares, do you guarantee fair weight across models or is it first-come-first-served? We have a mix of low-latency and batch models and want predictable tail behavior.
3) Observability: we need a dedicated dashboard link and an SLA over access to tracing logs for incidents.
4) Acceptance: we'll need the addendum to include an acceptance test window (30 days after signature) to validate that the pool meets the token-rate under our workload.

If you can bake those details into the final SLO language and send to DocuSign we can accelerate. Also send an explicit overage calculator example for a 4-hour spike so Procurement can budget.

Oliver

On a separate note: Priya and I are aligned on the 12-month term if the token-rate and fallbacks are explicit.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: redlines for DataSpan token-rate language

Folks — internal-only note (not to be sent to DataSpan as-is). Per Oliver's questions, I've drafted tighter SLO language and acceptance criteria. Key points:

- Measurement window: 1-minute moving average sampled at 10s intervals at the reserved-pool ingress agent; shortfall calculation uses the max of 1-minute and 5-minute moving averages to avoid transient noise.
- Aggregate vs per-model: contract to guarantee an aggregate token-rate only; fairness controls documented as recommended routing policy (we do not guarantee per-model isolation unless they purchase model-level reservations).
- Routing/fallbacks: define 'warm spare' as compatible model-variant with 80% overhead capacity available, automatic failover with priority tiers; DBR (degradation-by-rate) rules included to preserve low-latency paths.
- Acceptance test: 30-day window post-signature; DataSpan runs three representative load profiles provided in Appendix A; Redwood will validate observability and then countersign.
- Overage calc: example appended — 4-hour 2x spike on top of guarantee = estimated overage = X tokens * $0.012/1k => $Y (we'll replace X/Y with real numbers once we get spike profile).

Neha — can you confirm finance is comfortable with $0.012/1k for overage (we might consider a stepped discount at >10% overage)? Marissa — can you prep a Console dashboard link template we can point DataSpan at (read-only view for their SREs)?

Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

(Attachment: SLO_redlines_for_DS_v1.docx)

Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity increase — DataSpan

Oliver / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. We've incorporated your questions into the attached addendum and acceptance checklist. High-level callouts: 

- Explicit measurement: 250,000 tokens/sec = 1-minute moving average sampled at 10s intervals; shortfall uses the larger of 1-min and 5-min moving averages. Language is in Section 2.1.
- Aggregate assurance: guarantee is for aggregate reserved-pool throughput; routing policies and priority tiers for low-latency models are documented in Appendix B. If you want per-model reservations we can add that as a separate line item.
- Fallbacks and failover: warm spare behavior and graceful degradation rules in Section 3. Automatic routing will preserve low-latency priority tiers as defined.
- Acceptance testing: 30-day validation window post-signature with three representative profiles you provide. Redwood will provide the read-only dashboard link for monitoring and a tracing-snapshot export for incident post-mortems.
- Overage example: attached workbook calculates the 4-hour 2x spike scenario with the $0.012/1k token rate (see tab 'Overage Examples').

Next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance of the attached addendum (DataSpan_Renewal_Commitment_Draft.pdf) and the redlined TokenRate_Addendum_v1.docx.
2) We'll send the DocuSign envelope for signature (expected turnaround: 1–3 business days).

If you give the OK today I will kick off the DocuSign and loop Legal for countersignature.

Thanks — excited to keep supporting DataSpan's scale-up.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
